text:
ana: Quick PSA: our new Next + LangChain sample (starter-kit-llamachain) is causing confusing auth/retry behavior during onboarding. When users follow the README they sometimes see duplicate embedding calls + duplicated eval runs. Posting details so others are aware.
ben: Oof. Which flow specifically? Server-side index + client streaming?
cory: Yes, hybrid. The sample does an SSR pass to precompute vectors and then the client streams progressive answers.
nana: repro steps: clone starter-kit-llamachain, npm install, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env.local, npm run dev, open /demo. On first load you get 2x POST /v1/embeddings within ~10ms of each other and sometimes a second eval job queued.
ben: Do you have logs or network trace?
nana: Snippet below (sanitized):

```
2025-06-07T08:10:11.001Z INFO server: starting index build job=j-abc
2025-06-07T08:10:11.004Z DEBUG client: POST /v1/embeddings id=E-01 payload="intro paragraph"
2025-06-07T08:10:11.012Z DEBUG client: auth: refresh start
2025-06-07T08:10:11.020Z DEBUG client: POST /v1/embeddings id=E-02 payload="intro paragraph"
2025-06-07T08:10:11.050Z INFO eval-harness: job queued id=eval-42
```

ana: E-01 and E-02 are identical payloads. E-01 started the auth refresh, and E-02 arrived while refresh was inflight, which triggered another refresh attempt.
pat: Looks like two issues layered: 1) JS SDK lacks request coalescing for identical embedding inputs; 2) multiple client instances (SSR process + browser) each run their own refresh logic, and the SDK doesn't ensure a single-inflight refresh per instance when requests are concurrent.
ben: That matches a prior Python parity note: python sdk had coalescing/mutex behavior. We should list parity gaps in docs.
nana: Short-term mitigation I added to the sample: a tiny dedupe wrapper around embeddings (map key = JSON.stringify(input)) and lowered SDK retry attempts in lib/sdkClient.ts. Patch: gist: https://gist.github.com/example/dedupe-sample.
cory: Can you share the wrapper?
nana: Sure, gist snippet: 

```
const inflight = new Map();
export async function dedupeEmbed(input){
  const key = JSON.stringify(input);
  if(inflight.has(key)) return inflight.get(key);
  const p = client.embeddings.create({input}).finally(()=> inflight.delete(key));
  inflight.set(key,p);
  return p;
}
```

pat: Good pragmatic fix. But we should not rely on sample hacks forever. Filing SDK issue to implement two things: request coalescing (opt-in) for embeddings and a refresh mutex so concurrent 401s only trigger a single refresh flow per client instance.
sdk-bot: New tracker issue created: SDK-860 - js-sdk: opt-in embedding coalescing + single-inflight auth refresh per client (https://tracker.redwood.ai/SDK-860) :eyes:
ben: Also propose adding a short note in Developer Docs under "Hybrid pages" that explains three patterns: server-only indexing, client-only streaming, or hybrid with explicit dedupe. Include code snippet and test guidance.
cory: We added a Playwright e2e to the sample that asserts exactly one POST /v1/embeddings on initial full render. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-kit-llamachain/pull/19
ana: CI flagged flaky behavior in one of our runners where clock skew caused token expiry check to fail and trigger refresh more often. I added an extra README note recommending `ntp` or using mocked endpoints for test reliability.
pat: Also suggested a short dev helper script that mints a short-lived token for the local samples so new engineers don't have to create long-lived API keys while onboarding.
ben: Good call. Can someone add a short blurb in the sample README and link the SDK issue?
cory: I'll land the README update and reference SDK-860. We can revert the dedupe wrapper once SDK fix is merged.
sdk-bot: SDK team assigned to SDK-860 with priority P2; estimate 1 sprint.
nana: Thanks all. Filing follow-ups: 1) add DX doc on hybrid patterns; 2) add Playwright assertion to sample; 3) revert dedupe wrapper after SDK fix.
pat: Closing loop for now. If anyone else hits this in other starters (Next + LlamaIndex/LangChain/eval harness), ping here and tag @sdk-team. :raised_hands:
